meta.note: General, textbook-level description of oral solid dosage manufacture. Real processes differ by product, equipment and regulator. Defect causes are common textbook causes, not a diagnosis for a specific batch. Nothing here is a manufacturing, regulatory or GMP guarantee.

stages.name: Raw materials
stages.equipment: Quarantine storage, sampling booth, balances, analytical laboratory.
stages.purpose: Receive and approve active ingredients, excipients and packaging components before any use.
cpp: Correct identification and status labelling (quarantine, approved, rejected).
Storage conditions such as temperature and humidity.
defects: Out-of-specification or contaminated material entering the process.
inprocess: Identity testing of each container or delivery as required.
stages.gmp: Materials must be approved before use, traceable, and stored so that mix-ups and contamination are prevented.

stages.name: Dispensing
stages.equipment: Calibrated balances, dispensing booth with controlled airflow, labelled containers.
stages.purpose: Weigh or measure each material accurately for one batch.
cpp: Correct material and quantity, often with a second-person check.
defects: Weighing error or wrong material dispensed.
inprocess: Second-person verification of identity and weight.
Reconciliation of quantities against the batch record.
stages.gmp: Every weighing is documented and checked, and the area is cleaned between materials and batches.

stages.name: Granulation
stages.equipment: High-shear mixer granulator, fluid-bed granulator, or roller compactor for dry granulation.
stages.purpose: Turn fine powder into larger granules with better flow, compressibility and content uniformity.
cpp: Amount and addition rate of binder liquid (wet granulation).
Mixing time and impeller or chopper speed.
stages.gmp: Process parameters are defined, monitored and recorded, and the equipment is cleaned and verified between batches.

stages.name: Drying
stages.equipment: Fluid-bed dryer or tray dryer with temperature and airflow control.
stages.purpose: Remove liquid from wet granules to a defined moisture level.
inprocess: Loss on drying or moisture analyser readings.
stages.gmp: Validated drying conditions and documented endpoints protect product quality and stability.

stages.name: Blending
stages.equipment: Tumble (V, bin) blender or other blender, with sampling tools.
stages.purpose: Mix granules with remaining excipients, including lubricant, to a uniform blend.
cpp: Order of addition, particularly of lubricant.
inprocess: Bulk and tapped density where specified.
stages.gmp: Blend uniformity is demonstrated with a defined sampling plan, and blending parameters are fixed in the batch record.

stages.name: Compression
stages.equipment: Rotary tablet press with punches, dies and force monitoring.
stages.purpose: Compress blend into tablets of uniform weight, hardness and thickness.
stages.gmp: Frequent in-process checks with defined limits and action steps, plus tooling records, keep the run in control.

stages.name: Coating
stages.equipment: Perforated coating pan or fluid-bed coater with spray system.
stages.purpose: Apply a thin film for appearance, taste masking, protection, or to control release.
cpp: Spray rate and atomising air pressure.
defects: Picking and sticking of tablets to each other.
inprocess: Disintegration or dissolution of coated tablets where relevant.
stages.gmp: Coating solution preparation and spray parameters are controlled and recorded, and coating weight gain is verified.

stages.name: Filling
stages.equipment: Capsule filler, or liquid, powder or sachet fillers as relevant.
stages.purpose: Fill a measured dose into capsules or other primary containers.
stages.gmp: Fill accuracy is verified during the run, and rejected units are segregated and reconciled.

stages.name: Packaging
stages.equipment: Blister or strip packaging machine, bottle filling and capping, labelling, cartoning and serialisation equipment.
stages.purpose: Protect the product, identify it, and prepare it for supply.
cpp: Correct label, leaflet and batch information.
defects: Wrong or illegible batch and expiry information.
stages.gmp: Line clearance and label reconciliation are essential to prevent mix-ups, which are a leading cause of recalls.

stages.name: Quality control (QC)
stages.equipment: Analytical laboratory: HPLC, UV-Vis, dissolution apparatus, balances, microbiology laboratory.
stages.purpose: Test materials, in-process samples and finished product against specifications.
inprocess: Assay, dissolution, uniformity and related tests on finished product.
stages.gmp: Results are recorded contemporaneously and are traceable, and any out-of-specification result is investigated according to procedure.

stages.name: Quality assurance (QA)
stages.equipment: Document control, change control and deviation systems, audit programmes.
stages.purpose: Ensure the whole quality system works, including documentation, deviations, change control and training.
stages.gmp: QA is independent of production and holds authority over release and rejection decisions.

stages.name: Batch release
stages.equipment: Batch documentation, QC results, QA review; in many jurisdictions release by an authorised person.
stages.purpose: Confirm that a batch was made and tested in line with its approvals, and authorise it for supply.
cpp: All specifications met and deviations closed.
defects: Releasing a batch with unresolved deviations.
inprocess: Confirmation of test results and status.
stages.gmp: Only a qualified person or role authorised in the quality system may release a batch, and the decision is documented.

defects.name: Capping
cause: Trapped air in the powder during compression.
Excess fines, or too little binder.
Too much compression force or too fast a press speed.
defects.appearance: The top or bottom of the tablet separates like a cap when the tablet is ejected or handled.
prevention: Lower press speed and adjust compression force.

defects.name: Lamination
cause: Excess compression force or press speed.
defects.appearance: The tablet splits into two or more horizontal layers.

defects.name: Sticking
cause: Too little or poorly mixed lubricant.
Punch face damage or unsuitable surface.
defects.appearance: Material adheres to punch faces, and the tablet surface may look rough or pitted.
prevention: Dry granules to the target moisture.

defects.name: Mottling
cause: Uneven colour distribution from poor mixing.
Colour differences between the drug and excipients.
defects.appearance: Patchy or uneven colour on the tablet surface.
prevention: Use suitable colourants and dry gently.

defects.name: Weight variation
defects.appearance: Tablets from the same batch differ in weight, which can mean differing drug content.
prevention: Improve granule flow and size distribution.
Monitor weight frequently during the run.

defects.name: Orange peel
cause: Spray rate too high or atomising pressure too low.
Drying too fast so droplets do not spread.
defects.appearance: A rough, dimpled coating surface that resembles the skin of an orange.
prevention: Reduce the spray rate and increase atomising pressure.
